Level 5 · Assure

Level 5: Agentic Red Teaming and Assurance Professional

Plan authorised adversarial tests, validate control failures and report residual risk honestly.

Open the live courseSee pathways

Four core lessons live; engagement assessment in design

Who it is for
Penetration testers, red teamers, application security engineers and assurance specialists.
Before you start
Level 2 and Level 3 knowledge, or demonstrated penetration-testing experience.
Capstone evidence
A scoped red-team engagement against a purpose-built target, with an evidence pack, reproducible tests and a remediation retest.
How it is assessed
Observed engagement in the lab and a written report reviewed against a published rubric.

Modules and evidence

Each module ends in an artefact that goes into your portfolio.

ModuleYou will be able toEvidence
Engagement scoping and authorisationWrite scope, written authorisation, rules of engagement, test windows, safety constraints and stop conditions.Signed-off engagement plan (lab scenario)
Attack planningMap plans to the OWASP Agentic Top 10 and MITRE ATLAS techniques.Attack plan with technique mapping
Injection, poisoning and misuse evaluationsTest prompt injection, context poisoning, tool misuse, delegation abuse, inter-agent trust and supply-chain attacks.Reproducible test cases
Tool, sandbox and exfiltration testingTest APIs and tools, sandbox boundaries, exfiltration simulations and safe code execution.Boundary test results
Robustness and regressionRe-test across model, prompt, tool, retrieval and policy changes; defend against adaptive attackers.Regression suite
Evidence and reportingRecord preconditions, expected and observed results, impact, logs, reproduction steps and remediation retests; separate vulnerability, limitation, unsafe workflow, weak control and residual risk.Evidence pack and report

Live lessons for this level

4 lessons in the live course are currently mapped to this level.

  • 16Agentic red teaming and security evaluation
  • 21Break Your Own Defence: Adaptive Evaluation
  • 23Contain Your Own Agents and Evaluation Environments
  • 24Measure Poisoning: Memory, Tool Descriptions and Servers

The free lessons open without payment. Lesson order inside the course is by module, not by level.

Planned lessons

These lessons are specified but not yet published. They address gaps identified in the curriculum review.

  • P6Multi-agent failure and cascade testing Planned
    Delegation loops, trust propagation, shared memory, correlated failure, recursive tool calls, cost exhaustion and cascading action, with tests that expose them.
  • P7Agent-to-agent protocols: discovery, authentication and replay Planned
    Protocol security beyond MCP: discovery, authentication, authorisation, message integrity, replay, versioning and provenance of agents and servers.

External mapping

Related published credentials, as benchmarks and optional pathways only.

Credential or frameworkHow we use it
GIAC GAIPTOffensive AI testing benchmark with published objectives for direct and indirect injection, RAG, agents, MCP, API security and architecture flaws; verify presale status.
GIAC GOAARelated offensive AI analyst benchmark with practical AI-enabled offensive operations; distinct from agent-platform assurance.
CompTIA PenTest+General penetration-testing benchmark. Pin the exam version at release.

Offensive work is taught only in isolated lab environments with synthetic data, disposable credentials and audit logs. Nothing here is a route to testing systems you do not have written permission to test.
